P1.evidence: Best P1a in the batch — the setter was actually named and referenced: 'I already spoke to Kim, of course, you already gave me some ideas from where you're at, where you want to go.' Frame remains the standard three parts, missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Agreement obtained and the open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Age volunteered, not asked; height and weight never established at all on a prospect whose entire presenting problem is physical decline. Work covered thoroughly — fifteen years at an ethanol plant, the transition to trading, hours at the desk. Health conditions never asked: the scoliosis disclosure was entirely the prospect's own initiative, which the script scores as a miss no matter how useful it was. Injuries asked well — 'You mentioned you have like aches and pains that come up. What areas are we talking about?' Diet asked and pushed on — 'you're saying your nutrition is horrible... What is horrible for you?' — producing the DoorDash admission. Sleep never asked despite the prospect volunteering that his brother mocked how late he sleeps. Energy never asked despite exhaustion being a central theme.

P3.evidence: The strongest goals phase in the batch. 'What are those things?' at 00:20:25 was the single best question anyone asked in these ten files — it opened Tough Mudder, Bible study, the YouTube ambition, hunting recovery and the brain fog in one answer. The why was asked directly ('why do you feel like, yeah, I'm absolutely not okay with it getting worse?') and produced the nursing-home fear unprompted. The future-pace ran ('How would that be for you when you finally fix that?'). Drive-through to family, legacy and his father's decline all landed. Docked only because 'who else does that impact' was never actually asked — the nieces and nephews arrived on the prospect's own initiative — and there was no crisp reflect-back.

P4.evidence: 'You're telling your own dad that if he fixes his nutrition, it's going to be better. What stopped you from fixing your nutrition then?' is a textbook root-cause question and it worked — it produced the habit-loop explanation and, later, the disclosure about not caring. P4f ran in substance too: 'there is a reason that you're still doing DoorDash at the moment. There's a reason that you haven't started yet in those months of doing research. Is that correct?' The prospect named the gap himself: habit mode plus research paralysis. Prior gym history was only lightly explored, hence the partials on P4a and P4b.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran — 'would you be willing for staying the same for the next couple of years because you actually don't put in the effort that you need to put in?' — and the line in the sand ran: 'are you ready to go for it to actually say, okay, I'm done with sort of doing the research, I'm ready to sort of draw lines and then go for it?' — answered 'Yes, yes.' P5a is partial because the two-year picture was never asked for; the prospect built it himself in response to a different question, and the rep never made him articulate the cost of inaction against the $6,000 decision itself. 'Why not?' never ran.

P6.evidence: The blocker sweep ran cleanly: 'would there be anything that would make you not 100% certain of... getting more stamina, being able to just go out hunting without being drained?' — 'No, I got nothing in my life besides me that would stop that. I am my own worst enemy.' That answer was the whole call in miniature and the rep did not pick it up. The belief question was never asked in its scripted form, and the yes obtained was about readiness to start something, not about going all in on this. Hesitation surfaced immediately on price and the rep did not return to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: Offer declined on the call, so payment and onboarding were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran — 'outside of the investment being 6,000, do you feel like, yes, I am 100%, I do want to do this?' — and got 'yeah, I'm 100% into it.' No financial-picture questions ran, which was arguably correct here since the prospect volunteered 'It's not that I can't do it' and 'I don't have a problem with the price.' The genuine miss is the one financial fact that was sitting in the open and never used: he spends $30-35 per DoorDash meal on roughly 80% of his meals, which is several hundred dollars a month already being spent on the exact problem he is refusing to pay to fix.

'I'm not going to make a commitment on this call.' Two moves ran in substance: the worth question ('do you feel like it is worth $6,000 to you getting to that best shape?' — answered 'it's worth way more than $6,000') and the doubt probe ('could it be that it's just a little bit of a doubt there'). The rep also improvised a decent pattern-break frame. Never ran: 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?', the identity close, or the final 'are you sure? Nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?' The identity close was the obvious one to run against a man who had just described who he used to be at the gym every day.

SCRIPT GAP, and the sharpest instance of it in the corpus — 'I would believe that 70-80% of it can be found online.' Objection C assumes the blocker is capacity to pay; here the prospect explicitly said the price was fair and the blocker was perceived marginal value over free information. The rep improvised the correct answer once ('there is a reason that you're still doing DoorDash') and then let it go. There is no scripted sequence for pricing the execution gap rather than the information.

SCRIPT GAP — 'I need failures behind me before I commit.' A distinct objection with no play anywhere in the playbook: 'if I already tried here this last six months, and I tried, and I failed, if I've got failures all behind me, I would be way more susceptible to paying that right here and now.' He treats paid help as something that must be earned by prior failure, and cited his trading history as precedent. Neither OA, OC, OD nor OE addresses this. Proposed label: have_not_earned_help_yet.

MISSED CONTRADICTION rather than a script gap. At 00:05:00 the prospect said accountability was 'probably the biggest thing I need in my life... if I'm accountable to Trevor or somebody, I always pull through.' At 00:46:00 he said 'if I'm going to be my old self again, I don't need to be accountable to anybody.' Both statements are on the same recording forty minutes apart and the rep did not surface the contradiction, which was the single strongest available close.

notes: The best discovery in the batch — P3 and P4 are genuinely strong and the prospect opened up further than anyone else here — attached to a close that never used what discovery produced. Three loaded pieces of evidence went unfired: the accountability contradiction forty minutes apart, the several hundred dollars a month already going to DoorDash, and 'I am my own worst enemy' said in answer to the blocker question. Coach the transition from discovery to close, not the discovery.
